property_summary: Invariant: after a successful withdrawAll call by any user, that user's credit becomes 0 in the reference implementation; the mutant that performs the external call before zeroing credit can be re-entered to withdraw more than their credit leaving credit != 0 or causing extra balance changes, violating the invariant for some inputs and an adversarial reentrant caller.

For any caller and deposited amount, after withdrawAll completes the caller's recorded credit is zero (reference enforces zeroing before external call); the mutant that calls the external address before zeroing allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw again and leave credit non-zero, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after withdrawAll returns the depositor's recorded credit is zero (the reference clears credit before the external call; the mutant that calls the recipient before zeroing allows a re-entrant attacker to make an extra withdraw and leave credit non-zero for some inputs).

For any caller and any positive deposit amount, the reference contract always either (1) successfully sends the caller their withdrawn funds when withdrawAll is invoked (succeeding even if the recipient's fallback uses more gas), or (2) reverts only if the call itself fails in the reference; the mutant using transfer will instead revert or succeed differently when the recipient's fallback consumes more than the 2300 gas stipend — so there exists an adversarial recipient (a fallback that uses >2300 gas or reverts differently) and some deposit amount for which the mutant's withdrawAll behavior differs from the reference.

After a successful withdrawAll call, the contract's stored credit for the caller must be zero while the contract balance equals the prior balance minus the withdrawn amount; the mutant that zeros the credit before decrementing balance can leave contract balance inconsistent (e.g., underflow or wrong final balance) when the external call fails or reverts, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

After any deposit by a caller, calling withdrawAll either successfully returns the caller's deposited Ether and leaves c.credit[caller] == 0 and address(c).balance decreased by that amount; if the callee (recipient) reverts the external send, the reference contract still keeps its internal accounting consistent (credit reset only after successful balance decrement and thus does not lose track), whereas the mutant that zeroes credit before decrementing balance can cause the contract balance and stored credit to become inconsistent when the recipient reverts, breaking the invariant that after withdrawAll the stored credit equals 0 iff the contract sent the funds successfully.

For any caller and deposit amount, if the recipient reverts when receiving funds, the reference contract preserves its balance and stored credit (no funds are lost and credit remains nonzero), whereas the mutant that zeroes credit before decrementing balance can clear the caller's credit while leaving contract balance unchanged, breaking the invariant that address(c).balance == sum of credits.

For any depositor and any recipient behavior, after withdrawAll returns (either success or revert), the invariant that credit[caller] == 0 if and only if address(c).balance has been reduced by the withdrawn amount holds in the reference, but the mutant that zeroes credit before decrementing balance can break this relation when the external send reverts (credit cleared while balance not reduced).

After any deposit by a caller, if the recipient reverts when the contract attempts to send withdrawn funds, the correct contract preserves the caller's credit and contract balance (no credit cleared on failed send), whereas the mutant that zeros credit before decrementing balance can clear the caller's credit even when the external send reverts, violating that invariant.

For any caller and any deposited amount, calling withdrawAll always reduces the contract's recorded balance by exactly the withdrawn amount (so address(c).balance equals the recorded balance), whereas the mutant that omits decrementing balance will leave address(c).balance != recorded balance after some withdrawals.

For any actor and deposit amount, after the actor deposits and then calls withdrawAll, the contract's stored balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount (so recorded balance equals address(c).balance), but the mutant that omits decrementing the stored balance can leave the contract's recorded balance larger than its actual Ether balance for some inputs (actor and amount).

For any caller and any deposit amount, after the caller deposits funds and then calls withdrawAll, the contract's stored per-caller credit for that caller is zero (credit[msg.sender] == 0); the mutant that omits decrementing the global balance still zeros the caller credit but may leave the contract balance inconsistent—however both reference and mutant zero the caller credit, so instead we check the stronger invariant that after deposit then withdrawAll the contract's global stored balance equals the sum of all credits (i.e., recorded balance equals sum of mapping) — the mutant breaks this because it fails to decrement balance on withdraw and so recorded balance can exceed sum of credits.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after the depositor funds the contract then calls withdrawAll (which sends them their credited Ether), the contract's address balance equals the stored global balance variable; the mutant that omits decrementing the stored balance can make address(c).balance < c.balance() after a withdrawal.

After any sequence where one account deposits some amount and then withdraws, the contract's global stored balance equals the sum of all individual credits (i.e., c.balance() == sum of credit mapping); the mutant that fails to decrement the global balance on withdraw can make c.balance() larger than the sum of credits for some deposit/withdraw inputs.

For any depositor and any positive deposit amount, calling withdrawAll succeeds (call does not revert) and returns funds to the caller; the mutant flips the require to require(!callResult) so withdrawAll will revert when the external call succeeds, breaking this property for callers that can receive funds.
